Subject: Renewal proposal and forecast (2028-29)

Hi Diego / Grace / Karthik,

Thanks again for the trial support — usage has been higher than our sandbox estimates. We ran updated ARR scenarios (attached) and want to propose a renewal structure that (1) gets us predictable capacity for the next 24 months and (2) lets us accelerate consumption if product-market fit continues. High-level ask: a multi-year agreement with staged committed blocks and an optional triggered top-up that kicks in when monthly token consumption exceeds X% of committed baseline for two consecutive months.

What we are hoping for from Redwood:
- A clear ramp schedule (milestones and dates) so our finance team can model spend
- An agreed early-topup credit if we accelerate above the baseline (so we don’t pay full overage pricing)
- Co-term to our existing contracts (Mar 31) so it’s simpler for renewals

Attached: ARR_model_Fathom.xlsx with projection tabs; procurement will loop in the exact PO/terms.

Timeline: procurement needs a signed statement of work / MSA redline by Dec 10 to hit our internal renewal window. Can Redwood commit to a draft by EOD Dec 3?

Thanks,
Sophie

Hi Sophie — appreciate the model and timeline. We can meet procurement’s window. I pulled together three structured options that map to Fathom’s growth curve and keep operations predictable: short descriptions below, detailed numbers in the attached contract_draft_v3.pdf.

Option A — 24m anchored commitment (conservative)
- Annual committed token volume with 10% year-over-year uplift option
- Standard overage rates above committed baseline
- Early-topup credit: 20% off overage for any month where usage > 120% of baseline (applies to first two top-up months)

Option B — 36m stair-step (recommended for aggressive growth)
- Staged committed blocks every 12 months (e.g., 100T -> 200T -> 300T)
- Triggered acceleration: if usage exceeds 110% of current block for two months, the next block’s pricing applies retroactively to the month of trigger (limited to first acceleration per year)
- Co-term support to align to Mar 31 on year 3

Option C — Co-term + burst buffer (flexible ops)
- 24m base with a reserved burst pool for sudden spikes (monthly drawdown model)
- Bursts billed at reduced incremental rate; unused burst capacity converts to credits at quarter-end

Next steps I propose:
1) We share contract_draft_v3.pdf (attached) with the specific figures for Option B — it best matches your growth notes.
2) Grace will confirm SLO/burst guarantees and SLA credits; Karthik will validate runtime sizing and estimated burst consumption.
3) If those look good, we’ll prepare a DocuSign envelope and a single-co-term amendment to sync to Mar 31.

Can you confirm which option you want us to populate with exact pricing? We’ll aim to get a redlineable draft to you by EOD tomorrow (Dec 4) to meet Dec 10 procurement.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Diego: +1 415-555-0142

Subject: Re: Renewal proposal and forecast (2028-29)

Looping in a quick technical caveat re: Option B triggers — our runtime autoscaling can handle the step increases, but two notes for ops: (a) the KV cache warm-up for a big jump can add ~50–150ms tail latency for the first 10–20k requests post-trigger; (b) burst drawdown to the new block will not be instantaneous if customers use many large context-length flows. We can mitigate both by pre-warming on a canary route when the trigger threshold is hit (we offer a controlled 48-hour pre-warm window).

If Fathom is okay with a 48-hour pre-warm, we recommend Option B as operationally simplest and best unit economics.

—Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

- We need invoice cadence to match our fiscal quarter (quarterly invoices preferred)

Procurement (procure@fathomcloud.com) will send our standard redline doc — they prefer inline edits in the MSA. We’ll also need to route a short PO by Dec 12 to keep services uninterrupted.

On timing: if you can get a DocuSign ready with Option B numbers and Retro pricing callouts, we’ll circulate for signatures.

Sophie
